title: Project Foundation: Root Layout and Global Setup
description: Start here to understand the entire site's structure. The root layout sets up SEO, analytics, global styling, and theme configuration for all pages.
languageLesson: Next.js App Router: The root layout.tsx is the outermost page wrapper. All child routes render inside its <children /> placeholder. Use metadata export for per-page SEO.

title: Home Page Structure: Displaying Sessions
description: Learn how the home page imports session data and renders a grid of session cards using animations. This is the entry point visitors see.
languageLesson: React patterns: Data flows from lib/sessions.ts → page.tsx → SessionCard components. The sessions array is a single source of truth.

title: Core UI Animations: StaggerList and Reveal
description: Explore the reusable animation components that create the staggered entrance effect on the home page and throughout the site.
languageLesson: React Context and hooks: StaggerList uses React Context to coordinate timing between children. Reveal uses CSS animations with JavaScript delays.

title: Session Pages: The Guide Pattern
description: Session pages follow a consistent pattern for displaying guide content, prep materials, and bonus content. See how dynamic routing and content composition work.
languageLesson: Next.js dynamic routes: [slug] creates routes like /session/1, /session/2, etc. Each route uses the slug parameter to fetch the right content.

title: Content Management: Session Content Files
description: Content is stored in tsx files inside src/content/. Each session has prep, guide, and bonus content files that page components import and render.
languageLesson: TypeScript/TSX: Content files export React components and data objects. Use type safety with interfaces for structured content.

title: Reusable Content Components
description: Building blocks for rendering structured content: step cards, code blocks, tips, screenshots. These components are used across all session guides.
languageLesson: Component composition: Reusable content components accept props to customize text, code, and styling. This DRY principle scales across 10+ sessions.

title: Giveaway Landing Pages: Lead Capture System
description: The giveaway system drives lead generation. Each giveaway page has an auto-opening email modal, copy-to-clipboard buttons, and email verification.
languageLesson: Next.js nested layouts: The giveaways layout wraps all child routes with shared email-gate logic and metadata.

title: Email Capture Flow: Modals and Gates
description: Learn how the email modal appears, validates input, and submits data. The copy-email gate shows options to copy content or enter email.
languageLesson: React state management: Use useState for modal visibility, form status, and error messages. useEffect hooks manage side effects like focus and keyboard listeners.

title: API Routes: Lead Capture Backend
description: API routes handle form submissions, email validation, and data persistence. See how giveaway signups are recorded.
languageLesson: Next.js API routes: POST handlers receive form data, validate it, and store it. Use try/catch for error handling and return JSON responses.

title: Events System: Registration and Webhooks
description: Events (live workshops) have registration, waitlist, payment processing, and webhook handling. This is the business logic layer.
languageLesson: TypeScript interfaces: Define EventDefinition, Registration, and related types. Use type safety to prevent bugs in business logic.

title: Event Pages: Registration UI
description: Event pages display details, registration forms, media, and confirmation flows. See how UI flows connect to backend registration.
languageLesson: Next.js dynamic routes for events: /events/[slug] routes render event-specific content, pricing, and registration forms.

title: Payment Processing: Stripe Integration
description: Stripe webhooks handle payment confirmation, registration finalization, and abandoned checkout followups.
languageLesson: Webhook security: Verify webhook signatures before processing. Use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate processing.

title: Email Automation: Reminders and Followups
description: Automated emails for confirmations, reminders, abandoned checkouts, and location details. See the email infrastructure.
languageLesson: Email automation patterns: Idempotency keys, time-window calculations, and deduplication prevent duplicate sends.

title: Utility Helpers and Data Helpers
description: Learn the helper functions that support content rendering, date handling, copy-to-clipboard, and analytics.
languageLesson: Utility patterns: Keep business logic in pure functions. Use TypeScript type safety for helper function arguments.

title: Navigation and Global Components
description: Site-wide components: header, footer, particles background. These appear on every page and establish the visual identity.
languageLesson: Component reusability: Global components render consistently. Use CSS classes and theming for consistent styling across the site.

title: Participant Display: Carousels and Social Proof
description: Showcase participants and testimonials using carousels. Learn how to render lists of data with animations.
languageLesson: React component patterns: Use .map() to render lists. Manage carousel state with useState for current index.

title: Session Wrapup Pages: Celebrations and Demos
description: Wrapup pages celebrate session completions with participant reactions, takeaways, and next steps.
languageLesson: Page composition: Combine animations, carousels, and staggered lists to create an engaging wrapup experience.

title: Video Integration: Sticky Players and Embeds
description: Learn how to embed video content using React components that follow users as they scroll.
languageLesson: DOM manipulation in React: useEffect with scroll listeners to track video position. useRef to access DOM nodes.

title: Configuration and Data Flow
description: Understand how configuration files, environment variables, and data sources flow through the application.
languageLesson: Security patterns: Token generation, rate limiting, and secret verification. Environment variable usage for sensitive data.

title: Meta and SEO Setup: Sitemap and Robots
description: Configure search engine crawling and sitemaps to ensure all content is discoverable.
languageLesson: Next.js SEO: Use dynamic sitemap and robots.txt generation. Export metadata from pages for per-page SEO.
